candidates.source_name: Skupština Crne Gore — Pretraga zakona i drugih akata (zakoni.skupstina.me)
candidates.why_relevant: Official parliamentary legislative database of Montenegro. Holds the authoritative texts of predlozi zakona (bills) in procedure, adopted laws, amandmani, committee reports and sponsor documentation. Search supports filtering by act status (e.g. status=Povučen iz procedure, 'u proceduri'), so bill lifecycle and stage transitions can be tracked. Primary upstream of any banking/payments law long before the central bank issues guidance.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the app.php/akt/ search endpoint with status and date filters; harvest linked PDFs under /zakoni/web/dokumenta/zakoni-i-drugi-akti/ and diff against prior snapshots to detect new bills and stage changes.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language seed search + snowball from PDF hit into the search app

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the sjednice-radnih-tijela document tree; filter PDFs whose header contains 'Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet'; OCR/text-extract for bill names and dates.

candidates.source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore — javne rasprave (public consultation feed)
candidates.why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the proponent ministry for credit institutions, payment services, AML/CFT and fiscal legislation. This tagged news feed carries the javni poziv announcements opening each javna rasprava, with the consultation window (typically 20-40 days), the submission address and links to the Nacrt zakona plus obrazloženje. Confirmed live: entries observed for business-registration law amendments (10.08.2026) and budget/fiscal responsibility law (06.08.2026).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the tag-filtered listing (ou=13, tags=163) daily; extract article date, consultation open/close dates and attached document GUIDs; follow attachments to /dokumenta/{uuid} and wapi.gov.me download endpoints.

candidates.source_name: Program rada Vlade Crne Gore (annual government work programme)
candidates.why_relevant: Forward-looking pipeline document: lists, quarter by quarter, every zakon each ministry must deliver in the year, with the responsible obrađivač. This is the single best predictive artefact for 'which banking/payments law is coming and when' — e.g. Ministry of Finance items whose deadline slipped to Q2 2026. Complements the reactive consultation feeds.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Locate the annual Program rada Vlade PDF (usually adopted late Dec/Jan) via gov.me search; parse the tabular annex into (bill title, ministry, planned quarter) rows; re-check against the mid-year izvještaj o realizaciji.

candidates.source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette) — sluzbenilist.me
candidates.why_relevant: The constitutionally mandated publisher of record. Nothing is in force in Montenegro until it appears here; the gazette issue number and date fix the stupanje na snagu (normally the eighth day after publication, unless the law states otherwise) and any prelazne i završne odredbe transposition deadlines. Indispensable for date-accurate compliance timelines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the Aktuelnosti page for new issue numbers; because the root returned HTTP 403 to an automated fetch, use a browser-like client with proper headers, or fall back to the propisinet.me mirror for issue tables of contents. Full text archive is signposted to www.propisinet.me.

candidates.source_name: Ministarstvo evropskih poslova — usklađivanje propisa sa pravnom tekovinom EU (tabele usklađenosti)
candidates.why_relevant: Article 40 of the Poslovnik Vlade requires every bill submitted to Government to carry an Izjava o usklađenosti plus a Tabela usklađenosti, verified by the Ministry of European Affairs' Odsjek za usklađivanje propisa. These tables map each national article to the specific EU directive/regulation article (CRD VI, CRR III, PSD2/PSD3, AMLD) and state the degree of transposition — the single most precise indicator of what EU acquis a Montenegrin banking or payments bill is implementing.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest the Izjava/Tabela usklađenosti PDFs attached to bills on zakoni.skupstina.me (they are filed with the bill) and monitor MEP guidance pages; parse the tables into article-to-directive mappings. Note NGO reporting that these tables are not always proactively published — absence may require an FOI/slobodan pristup informacijama request.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on transposition instruments; snowball into an actual filed Izjava o usklađenosti PDF

candidates.source_name: Program pristupanja Crne Gore Evropskoj uniji (PPCG) — accession programme, Chapter 4 & 9
candidates.why_relevant: The national EU-accession programme sets, per negotiating chapter, the specific laws and bylaws Montenegro commits to adopt and the quarter by which. Chapter 9 (financial services: payment services, capital movement, AML/CFT) and Chapter 4 name the Ministry of Finance, CBCG, Komisija za tržište kapitala and the insurance supervisor as responsible institutions. It is the multi-year deadline backbone behind individual bills.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download each annual/biennial PPCG PDF; extract the Chapter 9 and Chapter 4 tables into (measure, legal act, responsible institution, deadline) rows; diff successive editions to spot slipped deadlines.

negative_findings.description: Searched for a dedicated national e-consultation portal at ekonsultacije.gov.me, by analogy with Serbia (ekonsultacije.gov.rs) and Republika Srpska (e-konsultacije.vladars.rs).
negative_findings.result_summary: No national Montenegrin portal at that address surfaced. The only 'eKonsultacije' hit for Montenegro is the Podgorica municipal platform (ekonsultacije.epodgorica.me). National-level consultations appear instead under the eUprava eParticipacija module (eusluge.euprava.me/eParticipacija/Rasprave/) and on each ministry's own gov.me news feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents the pipeline from being pointed at a non-existent endpoint and confirms that consultation monitoring in Montenegro must be ministry-by-ministry plus eUprava, not a single central register.

negative_findings.description: Attempted an automated fetch of the Official Gazette site http://www.sluzbenilist.me/.
negative_findings.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden, no response body. Search results nevertheless show live subpages (/aktuelnosti/) and an active institutional Facebook presence, so this is almost certainly bot defence rather than a dead site. Recorded as UNVERIFIED, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The gazette is the legally decisive source for entry-into-force dates. If automated access stays blocked, the collector must either use a browser-profile client or fall back to me.propisi.net mirrors, which introduces a licensing question and a lag risk.

negative_findings.description: Local-language search for a 2026 public consultation on a new/amended Montenegrin AML/CFT law (nacrt zakona o sprječavanju pranja novca i finansiranju terorizma).
negative_findings.result_summary: No 2026 javna rasprava for that act was found; hits were dominated by Croatian and Bosnian versions of the similarly-named law, plus existing Montenegrin consolidated texts on gov.me and scmn.me. Evidence of 2024/2025 amendments and a 2026 Constitutional Court decision published in the gazette exists, but no draft in consultation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: AML/CFT is a core banking-compliance topic; the absence of a current draft is itself intelligence (the file appears to be in an amendment-and-litigation phase rather than a rewrite), but the near-name collision with HR/BA statutes is a real precision hazard for any automated local-language query.

negative_findings.description: Montenegrin legislative vocabulary is shared almost verbatim with Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Republika Srpska ('predlog/prijedlog zakona', 'javna rasprava', 'Službeni list', 'skupština', 'zakoni u proceduri').
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple seed queries returned parlament.gov.rs, propisi.net (Serbia), vladars.rs, parlament.ba and Croatian sources ahead of Montenegrin ones. Reliable disambiguators observed: 'Crne Gore', 'Skupština Crne Gore', 'Vlada Crne Gore', the .me TLD, and the Montenegrin-specific spelling 'predlog' + 'sprječavanje'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without a country qualifier or .me domain filter, an automated local-language crawler for this cell will silently ingest Serbian and Croatian legislation and produce wrong transposition deadlines.

negative_findings.description: Investigated whether tabele usklađenosti (EU transposition correspondence tables), mandatory under Article 40 of the Poslovnik Vlade, are systematically published.
negative_findings.result_summary: Individual Izjava/Tabela usklađenosti documents were found filed alongside bills on zakoni.skupstina.me, but Montenegrin civil society has campaigned publicly for these tables to be published as a matter of course, implying coverage is inconsistent. No single searchable register of transposition tables was located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These tables are the highest-value artefact in the cell for mapping national provisions to CRD/CRR/PSD/AMLD articles. Inconsistent publication means the collector needs a per-bill harvest strategy and, potentially, freedom-of-information requests.

coverage_gaps.description: No structured/machine-readable interface (API, OAI/RSS, open-data dataset) was confirmed for either zakoni.skupstina.me or the Official Gazette. Collection would currently rest on HTML scraping and PDF harvesting.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe zakoni.skupstina.me for RSS/JSON endpoints behind the app.php search, check data.gov.me for a parliament or gazette dataset, and ask Skupština's IT/press service directly about a bulk feed.

coverage_gaps.description: The practical fallback for consolidated texts and gazette contents (me.propisi.net, katalogpropisa.me) is commercial. Terms of service and whether systematic retrieval is permitted were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Review both providers' ToS and pricing; if the gazette site stays bot-defended, budget a subscription rather than scraping, and record the licensing decision in the source register.

coverage_gaps.description: Within the law-making pipeline, several actors were identified by name but not yet resolved to a monitored URL: Sekretarijat za zakonodavstvo (legal-technical vetting and prečišćeni tekstovi), Zaštitnik/Ustavni sud (constitutional challenges to financial statutes, one such 2026 decision was referenced), and the Fiskalni savjet established in 2026.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and verify the landing pages for gov.me Sekretarijat za zakonodavstvo, ustavnisud.me decisions search, and the new Fiskalni savjet; add each as a distinct source with its own collection cadence.

coverage_gaps.description: No Montenegrin crypto-asset / MiCA-alignment bill was found in the pipeline; press reporting explicitly states Montenegro still lacks a crypto-asset law and EU alignment is pending. Similarly, no dedicated instant-payments or open-banking bill was identified separately from the Zakon o platnom prometu amendments.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Set standing watch terms 'zakon o kriptoimovini', 'kriptoaktiva', 'MiCA', 'instant plaćanja', 'otvoreno bankarstvo', 'PSD2/PSD3' against the Ministry of Finance consultation feed and the Program rada Vlade, so the bill is caught at first appearance.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin and derivative. Parliament offers an English entry point (zakoni.skupstina.me/25saziv/index.php/en/) and gov.me publishes some /en/ articles, but bill texts, consultation notices, gazette issues and transposition tables are Montenegrin-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat sr as the mandatory collection language and plan for machine translation of primary texts; do not rely on the /en/ mirrors for completeness or for date accuracy.

coverage_gaps.description: Bills adopted by skraćeni or hitni postupak bypass or compress public consultation, so the Ministry of Finance javna rasprava feed will not see them at all — they surface only at the Vlada session or directly on the parliamentary agenda.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not treat the consultation feed as the pipeline entry point. Monitor Vlada session communiqués and the parliamentary act register in parallel, and flag any act whose first observed stage is 'Predlog' as a possible fast-track.

brief: Montenegro's banking and payments rules are made along a well-defined and largely public chain: Ministarstvo finansija drafts a Nacrt zakona and opens a javna rasprava (its tagged gov.me feed and the eUprava eParticipacija module are the two indexes), the Vlada 'utvrđuje' the Predlog with an Izjava/Tabela usklađenosti verified by the Ministry of European Affairs, Skupština processes it through the Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet with every document filed on zakoni.skupstina.me, and Službeni list Crne Gore fixes the legally binding stupanje na snagu. The forward-looking deadlines sit in two planning documents — the annual Program rada Vlade and the Program pristupanja Crne Gore EU (Chapter 9, financial services) — which together predict which bills are coming and when. Two practical risks dominate: the Official Gazette site returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching (bot-defended, not confirmed dead — commercial mirrors me.propisi.net and katalogpropisa.me are the fallback), and Montenegrin legal vocabulary is near-identical to Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian, so every local-language query must be pinned with 'Crne Gore' or a .me domain filter. Bills passed by skraćeni/hitni postupak skip the consultation feed entirely, so the Vlada session communiqués and the parliamentary act register must be monitored in parallel rather than downstream.
